# messpunkt.io Partner API

> REST / OAuth 2.1 API that lets property-management ERPs read monthly consumption and meter-reading data from messpunkt.io on behalf of a landlord, plus an MCP server that lets landlords ask their own AI assistant about the same data. messpunkt.io is a metering platform for German real estate (sub-metering: heat, heat cost allocators, cold, warm and outdoor water).

**Status:** Preview · V1 release candidate `1.0.0-rc.3` · GA ships with the first pilot partner and is announced in the changelog
**Hosted at:** https://developer.messpunkt.io

This file follows the [llms.txt standard](https://llmstxt.org) — a Markdown index for LLMs and AI agents.

## Documentation

- [OpenAPI 3.1 spec (YAML)](https://developer.messpunkt.io/erp-api-openapi.yaml): the authoritative machine-readable contract
- [Reference documentation (Redoc)](https://developer.messpunkt.io/reference/): narrative documentation in English
- [Endpoint explorer (Swagger UI)](https://developer.messpunkt.io/swagger-ui/): request builder with try-it-out
- [Modern explorer (Scalar)](https://developer.messpunkt.io/scalar/): code samples in curl / JavaScript / Python / C#
- [Changelog](https://developer.messpunkt.io/changelog/): release history, including the rc.2 → rc.3 migration notes
- [ERP integration guide](https://developer.messpunkt.io/erp/): client registration, consent, PKCE, `iss` check, refresh rotation, revocation, DPoP, errors, rate limits
- [Error handling](https://developer.messpunkt.io/errors/): `application/problem+json` types and client actions
- [Plugin manifest](https://developer.messpunkt.io/.well-known/ai-plugin.json): OAuth + OpenAPI pointer for plugin-style integrations
- [Authentication & authorization flow diagram](https://developer.messpunkt.io/auth-flow.svg): Mermaid sequence diagram

## MCP server (for landlords' own AI assistants)

- Server URL: `https://mcp.messpunkt.io/v1` — part of V1, goes live together with the production REST API
- [MCP server reference](https://developer.messpunkt.io/mcp/): transport, auth challenge, scopes per tool, tool reference generated from `tools/list`
- [Landlord guide (German): Mit Claude, ChatGPT oder Codex verbinden](https://developer.messpunkt.io/connect/): connect steps per client, consent, limits, disconnecting
- Clients: Claude (claude.ai, Claude Code), ChatGPT, Codex and other MCP clients with OAuth support
- Read-only tools: `list_properties`, `get_property_overview`, `get_consumption`, `get_device_status`, `get_connection_info` — schemas in the [tool reference](https://developer.messpunkt.io/mcp/#tools)
- Same authorization server, consent screen and data rules as the REST API; tokens are issued for one resource (`aud`) and are not interchangeable between MCP and REST

## Capabilities (REST)

Under a single OAuth token scoped per Tenant **and** per Property (selection chosen at consent time):

- **Properties (Liegenschaften)** — `GET /properties`, `GET /properties/{id}`, `GET /properties/{id}/measuring-points` (every measuring point of a Property, including plant-room and main meters that belong to no unit)
- **Usage units (Wohneinheiten)** — `GET /usage-units`, `GET /usage-units/{id}` with inline Property summary for self-describing responses
- **Consumption per unit** — `GET /usage-units/{id}/consumption?from=…&to=…` returns, per MeasuringPoint and device installation window, month-end readings and the billable period consumption (meter replacements are explicit)
- **Measuring points** — `GET /measuring-points/{id}`, `GET /measuring-points/{id}/readings` (also for measuring points without a usage unit)
- **Token introspection** — `GET /whoami` returns tenant, scopes and the current `property_scope`

## Data rules

- **Monthly at the finest.** Readings are month-end values (`at` is a date); there are no daily, hourly or per-telegram values and no parameter to request them. Finer series per apartment would be a behavioural profile of residents.
- Bill `period_consumption.billable_value` (raw consumption × `factor`), summed over segments — not `last − first` reading. For a usage unit, bill `weighted_billable_value` (= `billable_value` × `unit_share`) from `/usage-units/{id}/consumption`.
- Shared Sectors: a measuring point shared by several units appears under each of them with its `unit_share`; `usage_unit_id` is the primary unit (highest share), `allocations[]` lists all units. Device values are never weighted.
- `status`: `measured` · `calculated` (interpolated month end, `is_synthetic: true`) · `substituted` (extrapolated end value; not produced today) · `missing` · `calibration_expired` (never bill; can be `is_synthetic: true`).
- `usage_unit_id` is `null` (and `allocations` empty) for a measuring point whose area is allocated to no unit, e.g. a total heat meter in a plant room. Such measuring points are not part of any unit or `/usage-units/{id}/consumption`; list them with `GET /properties/{id}/measuring-points`. `property_id` is always set. *(Breaking change in rc.3 — rc.3 is unpublished.)*
- `baseline_origin` on a segment says where the start value comes from; `assumed_zero` means the start value of a replacement heat cost allocator was not recorded and is assumed to be 0 — that segment's consumption rests on this assumption.
- `is_system_linked: false` marks a measuring point without an active system assignment: delivered with its values, while the landlord portal shows 0 for it — clarify before billing.
- Metrics: `heat` (kWh) · `hca` (unit) · `water_cold` · `water_warm` · `water_outdoor` (m3, not part of residents' water). `electricity` and `gas` are reserved — there are no readable devices for them today.
- `obis`, `resolution` and `external_ref` are always `null` today. Identify quantities by `metric` + `unit`.
- `installed_at` is `null` when the installation date is not documented — never a placeholder date.
- Difference meters: `is_difference_meter: true`, `active_device: null`, no readings. Pre-metering points (Vorerfassung) are not exposed.
- A missing value at the end of the range is never filled from an earlier month: `period_consumption.status` is then `missing` (unless `substituted`). A device removed inside the range ends with the value on the removal day.
- Invalid parameters (`limit`, `page_cursor`, `property_id`, dates, unknown `metric`, a range after the last completed month) return `400` with a `detail`; `500`/`503` carry no detail — retry with backoff.
- Sandbox data is static up to 2026-12-31 and contains no `substituted` values.

## Authentication

OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code + PKCE (S256), with `resource` (RFC 8707) and `iss` in the authorization response (RFC 9207). Tokens are issued for one Tenant. DPoP (RFC 9449) is supported and optional: a token obtained with a DPoP proof is bound to the key and must then be sent with a proof on every request. At consent time the landlord chooses all Properties (including future ones) or a selection — the token carries a `property_scope` claim (`"all"` or a list of UUIDs). Out-of-scope resources return `404 Not Found` (never `403`, to avoid leaking the existence of other Properties). Landlords can disconnect an application in the portal; it stops working within 60 seconds.

See the *Authentication* and *Authorization & Property scope* sections of the OpenAPI spec for the full flow and the sequence diagram.

## Usage for tool-calling LLMs

The OpenAPI 3.1 operation schemas map cleanly to:

- Anthropic Tool Use (Claude)
- OpenAI Function Calling / GPT Actions
- Google Gemini Tool Use / Vertex AI Function Calling

Typical queries an LLM can answer by calling one or two endpoints:

- "How much warm water did apartment WE 03 use in 2025 compared to 2024?"
- "Are any units in Musterstraße 12 showing unusually high heat consumption?"
- "When was the water meter in WE 03 last replaced?"
- "Which Properties does this landlord expose to our ERP?"

## Constraints for agent authors

- Always call `GET /whoami` after a token refresh and reconcile the current `property_scope`
- Problem `type` is `https://developer.messpunkt.io/errors/#<code>` (sandbox and production alike); branch on the fragment. `/oauth/*` answers `429` the same way, its other errors in the OAuth format
- Treat `404` on previously-known IDs as a scope revocation, not a retry condition; an ID that is not a UUID is also `404`
- The REST API has no fields for resident (Mieter) names or contact details; `UsageUnit.name` is the landlord's label for the unit
- Values are monthly at the finest; do not try to reconstruct finer series
- Rate limits (production and sandbox): REST `/v1/*` 300/min per connection (grant, the token's `sid`) after token validation, requests with an invalid token per caller address; `/oauth/token` and `/oauth/revoke` 60/min per `client_id` after client authentication, in addition 60/min per caller address; MCP 60/min per connection; `429` with `Retry-After`; counted in memory per server instance (best effort)

## Contact

- **Pilot partnerships & integration support:** [kontakt@messpunkt.io](mailto:kontakt@messpunkt.io)
- **Legal:** [Impressum](https://messpunkt.io/impressum) · [Datenschutz](https://messpunkt.io/datenschutz)

AI agents retrieving data on behalf of a landlord must respect the landlord's consent and the per-connection Property selection — do not attempt to bypass or broaden `property_scope` programmatically.
